captions_build.name: captions_build
captions_build.description: Use when word timings (words.json) exist and burn-in or sidecar captions are needed. Do not use without word timings (run audio_align or transcribe first). Returns captions.json pages plus SRT and VTT. Next skill: scene_plan_validate (S2) or render_preview.
captions_build.inputs: { words_path, preset, max_words_per_page?, emphasis?, emphasis_words?, combine_tokens_within_ms?, slot_width_px?, out_dir? }
captions_build.body:
# captions_build

Pages word timings into TikTok-style caption pages with `@remotion/captions` `createTikTokStyleCaptions`, then splits pages to `max_words_per_page`, re-splits pages wider than the caption slot, marks emphasis tokens and writes SRT and VTT sidecars.

## Run
`node toolkit/node/captions_build.mjs '{"words_path": "captions/ep001.words.json", "preset": "cube_pop_3word", "emphasis": "numbers", "slot_width_px": 800}'`

## Presets
See `caption-presets` in the toolkit data (also `get_schema`/`get_asset_sources` are unrelated; use `get_skill_file captions_build data/caption-presets.json` or the `platforms://presets` resource). Presets define font, weight, size at 1080 width, color, stroke or shadow, words per page, animation and vertical position. `mino_clean_3word` needs a verified TikTok Sans license; otherwise it falls back to Inter 600.

## Emphasis
- `numbers`: digits and number words.
- `keywords`: words in `emphasis_words` (take them from `script.lines[].emphasis_words`).
- `keywords_and_numbers`: both.

## Rules
- `slot_width_px` is the caption slot width in pixels at the spec width (layout slot w times width). Pages still flagged `overflow` must get fewer words or a smaller preset.
- Captions are hidden while on-screen text occupies the same area (set `caption_state: hidden_for_text` on that range).
- For talking-head footage use `caption_apply_style`, which adds face avoidance.

duration_estimate.name: duration_estimate
duration_estimate.description: Use when a script or a single line must be timed before TTS exists (scene_plan_create, script_tighten). Do not use when real word timings exist (use words.json). Returns est_ms per line from a per-voice words-per-second table. Next skill: scene_plan_create.
duration_estimate.body:
# duration_estimate

Counts spoken words (numbers, money and percents are expanded to their spoken form: "32" is "thirty two") and divides by the voice's words per second. Adds 60 ms per comma, 120 ms per full stop and 250 ms per SSML break.

## Run
- One line: `node toolkit/node/duration_estimate.mjs '{"text": "Day 5: 32 coins.", "voice_id": "local_default"}'`
- Whole script: `node toolkit/node/duration_estimate.mjs '{"script_path": "scripts/ep001.json", "project_path": "."}'`

## Calibration
The default is 2.5 words per second (a placeholder). After every `tts_generate`, the toolkit updates `voices.calibration.json` in the project with the measured rate (exponential moving average). Always pass `project_path` so the calibrated value is used.

## Rules
- Acronyms are spoken letter by letter; write them with dots or spaces in the script if timing matters ("A.I.").
- Keep digits in `display_text` for on-screen use; the spoken form is only for timing and TTS.

local_env_check.name: local_env_check
local_env_check.description: Use when starting any script skill on a machine for the first time, or when a script fails with ENV_MISSING. Do not use for validating a spec (use scene_plan_validate). Returns a JSON report of installed tools, what is missing and exact install steps for this OS. Next skill: project_create.
local_env_check.outputs: { ok, platform, found, missing[], optional_missing[], install_steps, notes[] }
local_env_check.body:
# local_env_check

Verifies that this computer can run the Scrollsmith script skills. Nothing is uploaded; no account is needed.

## When to run
- First time in a project, before `project_create`.
- Any time a script prints `{"code": "ENV_MISSING"}`.

## Steps
1. Make sure the toolkit is present locally (see the `toolkit` resource: fetch `toolkit://manifest`, write the files into `./toolkit/`, then run `npm install` inside `toolkit/`).
2. Run: `node toolkit/node/local_env_check.mjs`
3. Read `missing[]`. Each entry has `tool`, `why` and `install`. Tell the user the exact command for their OS and stop until the required tools exist. Required: ffmpeg, ffprobe, Node 20+, Python 3.10+ (Python only for audio and footage skills).
4. `optional_missing[]` lists whisperx, mediapipe, librosa, tesseract, yt-dlp and Chromium. Explain which skills need them (the `why` field) and let the user decide.
5. Repeat the `notes[]` to the user, including the Remotion license note: because rendering is local, the user or their organization is the Remotion licensee. Free for individuals and teams of up to 3; organizations of 4 or more may need a company license. HyperFrames (Apache 2.0) is the license-free engine alternative.

## Client capability
- Claude Code, Cursor and other clients with local code execution: full capability.
- Claude web or mobile chat without local file access: script skills cannot run. Say so plainly and offer the instruction skills (strategy, hooks, scripts, scene plans, text-only reviews).

## Output example
```json
{"ok": false, "platform": "darwin-arm64", "found": {"node": "v22.1.0", "ffmpeg": "ffmpeg version 7.1"}, "missing": [{"tool": "ffprobe", "why": "needed by every audio, caption, QA and render script", "install": "brew install ffmpeg"}], "optional_missing": [], "notes": ["..."]}
```

project_create.name: project_create
project_create.description: Use when the user starts a new series, channel or client project and no shortform-project folder exists yet. Do not use to change an existing project (edit project.json directly). Returns the created folder layout. Next skill: idea_generate (faceless) or goals_intake (branded).
project_create.inputs: { path, name, platforms?, aspect?, fps?, style_pack_id?, language?, brand_kit? }
project_create.body:
# project_create

Creates the local project folder. All later skills read and write inside it; nothing leaves the machine.

## Folder layout
```
shortform-project/
  project.json          name, platforms, defaults
  brand_kit.json        optional, brand_kit.v1
  tone_profile.json     from brand_voice_profile
  series/<series_id>.json
  specs/<spec_id>.v<N>.json
  footage/              raw footage, never uploaded
  assets/library.json   local asset index with license fields
  assets/ledger.json    license ledger for assets used in specs
  history/episodes.json past scripts and spec fingerprints (originality_check)
  renders/              previews, finals, receipts
  runs/<run_id>/run.json
```

## Steps
1. Ask for the project name and target platforms if not given. Defaults: platforms tiktok, reels, shorts; aspect 9:16; fps 30.
2. Run: `node toolkit/node/project_create.mjs '{"path": "./shortform-project", "name": "<name>", "platforms": ["tiktok", "shorts"]}'` (write the JSON to a file and pass the path if the shell makes quoting awkward).
3. Confirm the created paths to the user. If a brand kit exists, pass it as `brand_kit` so `brand_kit.json` is written.

## Rules
- Never store API keys in project.json. Providers read keys from environment variables.
- `local_only: true` is written into project.json and must stay true.

scene_plan_patch.name: scene_plan_patch
scene_plan_patch.description: Use when the user asks for a targeted change to an existing spec ("make range r03 faster", "swap the hook") or when scene_plan_validate reports errors. Do not use to build a spec from scratch (use scene_plan_create). Returns the new versioned spec path and the changed range ids. Next skill: scene_plan_validate.
scene_plan_patch.body:
# scene_plan_patch

Applies RFC 6902 JSON Patch operations to a spec and writes a new version file (`name.v2.json` -> `name.v3.json`). The old version is kept. Per-range hashes tell you which ranges changed so only those need re-rendering.

## Run
```
node toolkit/node/scene_plan_patch.mjs '{"spec_path": "specs/ep001.v1.json", "ops": [
  {"op": "replace", "path": "/timeline/2/end_ms", "value": 9000},
  {"op": "replace", "path": "/timeline/3/start_ms", "value": 9000}
]}'
```

## Writing ops
- Use the `path` from a validator error directly as the op path.
- Keep the timeline contiguous: when you change one range's `end_ms`, change the next range's `start_ms` in the same patch, and update `/format/duration_ms` if the last range moved.
- To remove a range: `{"op": "remove", "path": "/timeline/3"}` then fix the neighbours.
- To add a layer: `{"op": "add", "path": "/timeline/1/layers/-", "value": {...}}`.
- Never patch `meta.local_only`.

## After patching
Run `scene_plan_validate` on the new path. Report `changed_range_ids` so `render_preview` can reuse cached ranges.

scene_plan_validate.name: scene_plan_validate
scene_plan_validate.description: Use when a video_spec exists and must be checked before any render, and after every scene_plan_patch or apply_decisions. Do not use for footage QA after render (use qa_check). Returns {valid, errors, warnings, metrics} with a fix_hint per issue. Next skill: wireframe_render (if valid) or scene_plan_patch (if not).
scene_plan_validate.inputs: { spec_path, footage_index_paths?, ledger_path?, beats_path?, loop_seal_path?, wps? }
scene_plan_validate.outputs: { valid, errors: error.v1[], warnings: error.v1[], metrics }
scene_plan_validate.body:
# scene_plan_validate

Runs the JSON Schema check and every rule in the table below against a `video_spec.v1` file. Must pass (no errors) before `render_preview` or `render_final`.

## Run
`node toolkit/node/scene_plan_validate.mjs '{"spec_path": "specs/ep001.v1.json"}'`

For footage edits also pass `footage_index_paths` (one per source) so F1 to F4 can run. Pass `beats_path` for B1 and `loop_seal_path` for O1.

## Rules
| Rule | Check | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | Ranges sorted, no gaps unless allow_gap, no overlaps, first starts at 0, last end_ms equals duration_ms | error |
| T2 | Hook range starts at 0 and ends by 3000 ms | warn |
| T3 | Faceless range longer than 4000 ms | warn |
| T4 | Narration fits the range (+/-150 ms) at the voice's words per second | error |
| S1 | Every text layer slot inside the safe-zone preset | error |
| S2 | Caption slot inside universal_relaxed; captions never overlap a text slot | error |
| L1 | Body text at least 48 px, titles at least 72 px (house rule) | warn |
| L2 | At most 3 on-screen words per second per range (house heuristic) | warn |
| P1 | A visual change at least every 2.5 s (house heuristic) | warn |
| A1 / F6 | Every asset_id in the ledger, commercial_ok true, music not high Content ID risk | error |
| A2 | Shorts over 60 s with non YouTube Audio Library music | warn |
| B1 | Snapped cuts within 1 frame of the beat grid | warn |
| O1 | Loop enabled: loop_seal report present and SSIM at least 0.92 | error |
| C1 | CTA exists and sits in the second half unless cta_policy early | warn |
| F1 | Footage cuts never inside a word | error |
| F2 | Every footage cut has an audio crossfade | error |
| F3 | Face bbox inside the safe zone after reframe | error |
| F4 | Captions never cover the face | error |
| F5 | hook_first on: a hook range in the first 3 s | warn |
| F7 | Cloned or changed voice requires meta.voice_consent true | error |

House heuristics (T3, L1, L2, P1) are defaults, not platform rules. Calibrate them with the user's own analytics.

## How to fix
- Read `errors[]` in order. Each has `path` (JSON pointer) and `fix_hint`. Apply the hint with `scene_plan_patch` (RFC 6902 ops), then validate again. Two passes usually suffice; if a third pass still fails, show the remaining errors to the user instead of guessing.
- Warnings do not block rendering. Mention them to the user once.

## Metrics
`metrics` includes range count, average range length, visual changes per minute and hook end time. Quote them when asking the user to approve the plan.

variation_pick.name: variation_pick
variation_pick.description: Use before scene_plan_create for every new episode of a series, to choose palette, camera and other variation axes so episodes do not look mass-produced. Do not use for one-off videos without a series. Returns seeded picks that avoid the last N episodes. Next skill: scene_plan_create.
variation_pick.body:
# variation_pick

Seeded PRNG (mulberry32) over the style pack's `variation_axes`, excluding values used in the last N episodes recorded in `history/episodes.json`. This is the main lever against the "repetitive content" and "originality" platform policies.

## Run
`node toolkit/node/variation_pick.mjs '{"pack_manifest_path": "packs/cubestory/manifest.json", "history_path": "history/episodes.json", "seed": 1042}'`

## Rules
- Use the episode seed (`meta.seed`) so the pick is reproducible.
- Write the picks into `style.variation` of the spec and record them in `history/episodes.json` after the render so the next episode avoids them.
- If a pack has no `variation_values` for an axis, the palette variants from `tokens.palette_variants` are used.

asset_library.v1.title: Local asset library index
asset_library.v1.description: Index of the user's own folders. Stored locally only. license defaults to unknown, which blocks final render.

license_id.description: e.g. CC0, CC-BY-4.0, OFL-1.1, owned, unknown

edit_decision.v1.title: Editing decision registry entry
edit_decision.v1.description: A decision is data: a detector (how to find the moment) plus an effect (what to do) plus parameters plus applicability.

default_on.description: Whether a style with no opinion should enable this decision

edit_style.v1.title: Edit style profile
edit_style.v1.description: Output of edit_style_create from one reference video. Measured values come from scripts only; the assistant writes notes_md and picks decisions. The reference video itself is never stored.

notes_md.description: Human-readable style guide the assistant reads

error.v1.title: Tool error
error.v1.description: Printed by every toolkit script on failure and used by validators for each issue.

path.description: JSON pointer into the offending spec field

fix_hint.description: One actionable sentence the assistant can follow

footage_index.v1.title: Footage index
footage_index.v1.description: Output of footage_ingest, written next to the footage. Never uploaded.

bbox_norm.description: x, y, w, h normalized 0 to 1

transcript_pack_path.description: Compact timestamped text for the assistant (about 10 to 20 KB), never raw video

run.v1.title: Local run state
run.v1.description: Written by long local scripts under runs/<run_id>/run.json so a run can be resumed or polled by reading the file.

text.description: Spoken text. Numbers may be digits; TTS expands them.

display_text.description: Optional on-screen form when it differs from the spoken form

status.description: manifest_only packs ship tokens and component contracts but no component code yet

video_spec.v1.title: Video spec (per-second scene plan)
video_spec.v1.description: One contract for faceless videos and footage edits. Faceless videos fill layers with generated components; footage edits also fill sources and per-range source_* fields.

voice_consent.description: Required true when a cloned or changed voice is used (rule F7)

retention_purpose.description: Why a viewer keeps watching here, e.g. open loop: what happens at day 30

narration_est_ms.description: Estimated or measured narration duration for rule T4

reason.description: Why this segment is kept (footage edits)

slot.description: Named region from the layout preset, e.g. top_title, center_visual, bottom_caption

text.description: Text content for text layers (used by S1 and L1 measurements)

font_px.description: Font size at the spec width, for L1

words.v1.title: Word timings
words.v1.description: Remotion Caption shape: text has a leading space, times in ms.

caption-presets.$comment: Caption presets. Sizes are px at 1080 width. mino_clean_3word is seeded from a public skill description (one verified style, not a vendor's full product style); TikTok Sans licensing must be verified before bundling, so the preset names a metric-compatible fallback.

mino_clean_3word.notes: Talking-head vertical video; kept clear of TikTok and Reels buttons. Verify TikTok Sans license before bundling.

hooks-taxonomy.$comment: Templates are paraphrased patterns, not measured performance. hook_library_search returns a pattern plus a paraphrase, never a creator's text for verbatim reuse.

types.template: What happens if you [X] every day for [N] days?
types.visual_hint: Show the starting state and a hidden end state
Numbered header with the last item blurred

types.template: Start at the climax, then: Let me back up.
types.visual_hint: Open on the most dramatic frame

types.template: No words; an impossible visual in frame 1.
Bet you can't [task] before this ends.

grading_rubric.clarity: One idea, understood on first hearing
grading_rubric.specificity: Concrete nouns and numbers, no vague promise
grading_rubric.curiosity: Opens a loop the payoff closes
grading_rubric.visual_support: A frame-0 visual that carries the hook without sound
grading_rubric.time_to_proposition: Proposition is clear within 3 s (TikTok creative best practices, ads context)

layouts.$comment: Layout presets. Coordinates are normalized 0 to 1 on the frame (x, y, w, h). Slots are named and resolved by style packs. 9:16 is the canonical definition; other aspects list adaptations.

adapt.1:1: title 0.06 to 0.18, visual 0.18 to 0.78, caption 0.80 to 0.92
adapt.16:9: title left third, visual right two-thirds, caption lower band

layouts.notes: The incoming item band at 0.66 is outside the strict safe zone: animate it in from the right inside the safe zone instead of holding text there.

layouts.use: Fake texts, DM stories (label as fiction)

layouts.notes: Caption shifts within universal_relaxed to avoid the face bbox (rule F4).

motion-primitives.$comment: All primitives are frame-pure functions: primitive(frame, fps, start, duration, params, seed). Never use Date.now() or Math.random(); use the seed.

groups.implementation: Remotion interpolate and spring; text measuring for layout
interpolate with an exponential curve for doubling stories
R3F camera props driven by frame; 2D via CSS transform
Seeded RNG; instanced meshes in R3F

platform-rules.$comment: Versioned, date-stamped platform policies used by policy_check and the validator. Status per entry: VERIFIED (read on an official page), SECONDARY, UNVERIFIED. Policies change: re-verify before relying on them.

rules.text: Put the hook in the first 6 s; introduce the proposition in the first 3 s.
rules.source: TikTok Ads Help Center creative best practices

rules.text: Tracks above 120 BPM are recommended for higher view-through rate.
Realistic AI-generated content must be labeled; TikTok reads C2PA Content Credentials and auto-labels; auto labels cannot be removed.
Square or vertical videos up to 3 min count as Shorts (uploads from Oct 15, 2024).
YouTube Audio Library tracks do not receive Content ID claims; Shorts Audio Library music may cover up to 90 s of a 3 min Short.
1 to 3 min Shorts with an active Content ID claim were blocked; a reported change effective Sept 24, 2026 says they may remain playable.
Monetization policy covers repetitive or mass-produced (inauthentic) content; renamed July 15, 2025. A further July 2026 rename is reported but unverified.
rules.source: YouTube statement via Search Engine Journal

rules.text: Reels up to 3 min are eligible for recommendation (Jan 2025).
Only the original of identical content is recommended; aggregators are removed from recommendations; visible third-party watermarks reduce recommendation.
rules.source: Instagram announcement via TechCrunch; Instagram creators blog

rules.text: Accounts repeatedly posting others' content they did not create or materially enhance (10 or more times in 30 days per the Apr 30, 2024 announcement) are not shown in recommendations; a 2026 update reportedly uses 'primarily' instead of a number.
rules.source: Instagram announcement; 2026 update via secondary report

rules.text: Do not use: '71% decide in 3 s', 'algorithm decides at 1.5 s', '2.5 s clip length = 35% higher completion'. No primary source found.

policy_check_flags.ai_label_required: meta.ai_disclosure == realistic_ai or any asset with ai_generated and realistic output
policy_check_flags.music_risk: music asset content_id_risk is high or unknown; Shorts over 60 s with non YouTube Audio Library music
policy_check_flags.reused_content_risk: sources that are third-party footage or background_footage not owned or licensed
policy_check_flags.third_party_watermark: OCR finds another platform's watermark or handle on sampled frames
policy_check_flags.voice_consent: voiceover.cloned_or_changed is true and meta.voice_consent is not true
policy_check_flags.claims: script.claims with status unverified or false
policy_check_flags.endorsement_implication: overlay of a real person or logo next to a product claim

render-presets.$comment: Bitrates are not platform-verified; use CRF 18 to 20 masters. Loudness targets of -14 LUFS and -1 dBTP are common conventions, not official platform numbers.

safe-zones.$comment: 1080x1920 pixel insets. Platforms rarely publish exact values and third-party measurements conflict. Versioned data, not platform guarantees. Validate hard UI text against universal_strict; allow captions inside universal_relaxed.

voices.$comment: Voice catalog with calibrated words per second. wps starts at 2.5 as a placeholder until duration_estimate updates it from real tts_generate outputs (exponential moving average).

voices.notes: Local TTS (Kokoro or Piper; verify license before use). Free fallback.
Uses the user's own ELEVENLABS_API_KEY. Model Multilingual v2 or Flash v2.5.

audio_voice.name: Light voice denoise
audio_voice.rationale: RNNoise (arnndn) at low strength removes hiss without the underwater artifact.

audio_voice.name: Loudness target
audio_voice.rationale: -14 LUFS integrated and -1 dBTP are common conventions, not verified platform numbers.

audio_voice.name: Voice EQ presence preset
audio_voice.rationale: High-pass at 80 Hz, small dip at 300 Hz, lift at 3 kHz: clearer on small speakers.

audio_voice.name: Room-tone fill after silence cuts
audio_voice.rationale: Hard digital silence between cuts sounds like a glitch; fill with the recording's own noise floor.

audio_voice.name: Match loudness between speakers
audio_voice.rationale: Two mics rarely match; normalize per speaker before the mix.

brand_graphics.name: Logo bug
brand_graphics.rationale: Safe-zone-aware corner from the brand kit. Never other apps' logos or watermarks (Instagram downranks visible third-party watermarks).

brand_graphics.name: Lower third at first appearance
brand_graphics.rationale: Name and title once per speaker; needs the speaker name from the brand kit or the user.

brand_graphics.name: Brand colors on captions
brand_graphics.rationale: Emphasis color = brand accent; body stays white for contrast (L1).

brand_graphics.name: Intro card
brand_graphics.rationale: Intros eat hook time: off for short-form by default.

brand_graphics.name: Outro and end card with CTA
brand_graphics.rationale: Handle, one CTA, brand colors; at most 1.5 s in short-form.

brand_graphics.name: Progress bar
brand_graphics.rationale: Signals the video is short; place inside the safe zone, not at the frame edge.

broll_overlay.name: B-roll on noun phrases
broll_overlay.rationale: Nouns the assistant extracts from the transcript pack become b-roll cues; assets from the user's library or stock_search, registered in the ledger.

broll_overlay.name: Screenshot of a named product or site
broll_overlay.rationale: Show the thing being named; the user supplies or captures the screenshot.

broll_overlay.name: Logo, person or meme overlay on mention
broll_overlay.rationale: Images of real people carry editorial-use risk and must never imply endorsement; memes carry copyright risk. License flag stored per asset (overlay_image_search).

broll_overlay.name: Sticker or GIF on the punchline
broll_overlay.rationale: Prefer user-owned stickers; Giphy and Tenor terms are not verified.

broll_overlay.name: PiP of a source clip
broll_overlay.rationale: Reaction and commentary formats; keep inside the safe zone.

broll_overlay.name: Arrow or highlight callout
broll_overlay.rationale: Deictic words usually point at something on screen.

broll_overlay.name: No b-roll over emotional moments
broll_overlay.rationale: The face carries the emotional peak; keep it on screen.

captions.name: Words per caption page
captions.rationale: 2 to 3 words per page reads at speech pace on a phone; more becomes subtitles.

captions.name: Clean talking-head preset
captions.rationale: White, soft shadow, no animation: the least distracting default for a person on camera.

captions.name: Pop-in preset
captions.rationale: Energetic formats tolerate animated captions; talking heads mostly do not.

captions.name: Karaoke highlight preset
captions.rationale: Word-level highlight helps retention when the narration is dense.

captions.name: Emphasis color on numbers and keywords
captions.rationale: Numbers and the script's emphasis_words carry the claim; color them, nothing else.

captions.name: Emoji accents
captions.rationale: One emoji per page at most; off for professional brands (brand kit decides).

captions.name: Shift captions off the face
captions.rationale: Rule F4: captions never cover the face; shift within universal_relaxed, else fewer lines, else hide.

captions.name: Hide captions during on-screen text
captions.rationale: Two text blocks at once halves reading speed (rule L2, S2).

captions.name: Sidecar captions for long-form
captions.rationale: YouTube long-form viewers toggle captions; burned-in text fights the player UI.

captions.name: Minimum page display time
captions.rationale: Pages shorter than about 350 ms flicker; merge them with the neighbour.

color_look.name: Apply a LUT
color_look.rationale: FFmpeg lut3d with a user-supplied .cube; none by default.

color_look.name: Contrast and saturation bump
color_look.rationale: Small lift; phone screens already saturate.

color_look.name: Skin-tone protect
color_look.rationale: Saturation bumps drift skin orange; mask the skin hue range.

color_look.name: Vignette
color_look.rationale: Draws the eye to the center; subtle.

color_look.name: Film grain
color_look.rationale: Hides banding in gradients; costs bitrate.

color_look.name: Black and white for emphasis
color_look.rationale: One desaturated beat on the key line; more than once is a gimmick.

cut_pacing.name: Remove dead air

max_gap_ms.description: Silences at least this long are cut

keep_ms.description: Breathing room kept around each cut

cut_pacing.rationale: Dead air is the first thing viewers scroll past; keeping a short pause preserves natural rhythm.

cut_pacing.name: Remove filler words

words.description: Per-language filler list. Add 'like' or 'you know' only if the speaker overuses them.

cut_pacing.rationale: Fillers read as unprepared; cutting them is the cheapest perceived-quality gain.

cut_pacing.name: Trim audible breaths
cut_pacing.rationale: Softer alternative to silence_remove for calm formats: shortens breath gaps instead of removing them.

cut_pacing.name: Jump cut on sentence boundaries
cut_pacing.rationale: Cuts on sentence ends feel invisible; cuts mid-sentence feel like mistakes (rule F1).

cut_pacing.name: Trim dead air at start and end
cut_pacing.rationale: A video must start on the first word; the hook clock starts at frame 0.

cut_pacing.name: Max single shot length by format
cut_pacing.rationale: When no cut is available, a visual change (punch-in or crop change) must happen within the max shot length (rule P1).

cut_pacing.name: Hook-first reorder
cut_pacing.rationale: Open on the strongest self-contained line; keep or drop the original intro (rule F5).

cut_pacing.name: Speed up slow sections slightly
cut_pacing.rationale: A 5% speed-up is below the threshold most viewers notice and recovers time without cuts.

export_platform.name: Reels preset
export_platform.rationale: Reels up to 3 min are eligible for recommendation.

export_platform.name: Shorts preset
export_platform.rationale: Shorts up to 3 min; music rules differ over 60 s (rule A2).

export_platform.name: Universal strict safe zone
export_platform.rationale: One render that is safe on all three vertical platforms; validate hard UI text against it, captions against universal_relaxed.

export_platform.name: Cover frame from the hook
export_platform.rationale: cover_frame renders a still of the hook range at 1080x1920 and 1280x720.

export_platform.name: Sidecar SRT and VTT
export_platform.rationale: Always ship SRT and VTT with the package even when captions are burned in.

export_platform.name: Loudness normalize on export
export_platform.rationale: Two-pass loudnorm; targets are conventions, not verified platform numbers.

export_platform.name: One variant per platform
export_platform.rationale: multi_platform_resize re-validates the safe zone per target.

format_specific.name: Talking-head defaults
format_specific.rationale: The default bundle an edit style starts from when it has no opinion.

format_specific.name: Faceless defaults
format_specific.rationale: Pacing and SFX density for code-driven video.

format_specific.name: Ad or UGC beat map
format_specific.rationale: Problem, demo, proof, offer, CTA; captions on; CTA end card; claims list runs through fact_check.

format_specific.name: Cursor zoom on clicks
format_specific.rationale: Zoom to the click target; blur sensitive regions found by OCR (emails, keys).

format_specific.name: Click highlight
format_specific.rationale: Ring around the cursor on each click.

format_specific.name: Idle-time trim
format_specific.rationale: Loading and typing stretches get sped up instead of cut so context survives.

format_specific.name: Podcast speaker cards and waveform
format_specific.rationale: Speaker card on each change; waveform layer under the captions; cut-follow-speaker reframe.

format_specific.name: Long-form chapters and retention resets
format_specific.rationale: Chapter title at each topic shift; a visual reset at least every 90 s.

format_specific.name: Long-form cold open
format_specific.rationale: Up to 20 s of the best moment before the intro card.

hook_structure.name: Cold open on the strongest line
hook_structure.rationale: Rule F5; the assistant picks the line and verifies it is self-contained and truthful.

hook_structure.name: Text hook over frame 0
hook_structure.rationale: Most feeds start muted; the hook must read without sound.

hook_structure.name: Pattern-interrupt visual
hook_structure.rationale: A motion or scale event in the first 0.8 s.

hook_structure.name: Tease then context reorder
hook_structure.rationale: Show a glimpse of the payoff, then back up (in media res).

hook_structure.name: Proposition by 3 s check
hook_structure.rationale: TikTok creative best practices (ads context): proposition in the first 3 s. Enforced by rule T2.

hook_structure.name: Open loop label on the hook
hook_structure.rationale: Small label naming what the viewer will get at the end (wait for day 30).

music.name: Pick track by mood and BPM
music.rationale: From the user's own library only (music_select); above 120 BPM for energetic formats per TikTok ads guidance.

music.name: Music level under voice
music.rationale: 16 to 20 dB under the voice keeps speech intelligible on phone speakers.

music.name: Duck on speech
music.rationale: Sidechain compression on the voice; release about 250 ms.

music.name: Drop at the hook end
music.rationale: The first musical event lands where the hook resolves.

music.name: Fade out at the end
music.rationale: Non-looping videos end on a fade, not a hard stop.

music.name: Bar-aligned loop
music.rationale: Looping videos cut the music on a bar boundary so the seam is inaudible (loop_seal).

music.name: Silence under the key line
music.rationale: Dropping the music for the payoff line makes it land harder.

sfx.name: Whoosh on transitions
sfx.rationale: From the user's SFX library; asset chosen by sfx_place.

sfx.name: Pop on text-in
sfx.rationale: Every on-screen text entry gets a short pop; never over a key word.

sfx.name: Riser into the reveal
sfx.rationale: A 1 to 2 s riser before the payoff range.

sfx.name: Click on counter ticks
sfx.rationale: Number rolls read as physical when each step clicks.

sfx.name: Impact on zoom punch
sfx.rationale: Pair the loudest punch-ins with a soft impact; most punch-ins stay silent.

transitions.name: Hard cut by default
transitions.rationale: Cuts are invisible; every other transition is a stylistic choice that must earn its place.

transitions.name: Whip pan on topic change
transitions.rationale: Marks a section change without a title card.

transitions.name: Flash on reveal
transitions.rationale: One flash per video, on the payoff.

transitions.name: Match cut on repeated shapes
transitions.rationale: Carry a shape or position across the cut; also the best loop bridge.

transitions.name: Glitch (rare)
transitions.rationale: Glitch reads as dated when overused; at most once.

zoom_framing.name: Punch-in on emphasis words
zoom_framing.rationale: A punch-in on the stressed word adds a visual change where the audio already has energy. Never in the first or last 300 ms of a shot; face stays inside the safe zone (F3).

zoom_framing.name: Alternate punch-in on sentence starts
zoom_framing.rationale: Gentler pacing device for calm formats.

zoom_framing.name: Slow push on long shots
zoom_framing.rationale: A barely perceptible push keeps a static shot alive.

zoom_framing.name: Alternate A/B crop on each cut
zoom_framing.rationale: Two framings from one camera simulate a two-camera shoot and hide jump cuts.

zoom_framing.name: Auto-reframe to vertical with subject tracking
zoom_framing.rationale: 16:9 sources need a smoothed crop path that follows the speaker; two speakers use split-screen or cut-follow-speaker.

zoom_framing.name: Headroom rule
zoom_framing.rationale: Eyes at about one third from the top; too much headroom reads amateur.

zoom_framing.name: Re-center on speaker change
zoom_framing.rationale: Follow the active speaker instead of a wide two-shot in vertical.

faceless._intro:
# Faceless code-driven rulebook

Videos generated from a `video_spec` with a style pack. House rules.
faceless.workflow: idea_generate -> script_write -> hook_generate -> hook_grade -> script_tighten (checkpoint: script) -> variation_pick -> scene_plan_create -> tts_generate -> audio_align -> music_select -> beat_detect -> beat_sync_apply -> sfx_place -> captions_build -> loop_seal (if loop) -> scene_plan_validate -> wireframe_render (checkpoint) -> render_preview -> qa_check (checkpoint) -> originality_check -> policy_check -> render_final -> qa_check -> cover_frame -> metadata_write -> export_package.
faceless.structure:
- Beats: hook (0 to 3 s), context, escalation x N, payoff, optional twist, CTA in the last 25 percent, loop_bridge if looping.
- Every range states its `retention_purpose` (an open loop, a reveal, a question). If you cannot name one, merge the range.
- Max range 4 s. Visual change at least every 2.5 s.
faceless.visuals:
- One layout per range from `layouts://index`; text only in safe-zone slots.
- Body text at least 48 px, titles at least 72 px at 1080 width; contrast at least 4.5:1.
- At most 3 on-screen words per second. Captions hide while a title occupies the same area.
- Variation: palette, camera and motion axes change per episode (`variation_pick`); the same template every day is penalized by platforms.
faceless.audio:
- Narration drives timing; snap cuts to beats only when the narration still fits.
- Music above 120 BPM for energetic formats (TikTok ads guidance), ducked -12 dB under narration, drop at the hook end.
- Loudness -14 LUFS, -1 dBTP.
faceless.loop: - `state_match`: the last range ends in frame 0's state; verify with SSIM at least 0.92 between the first and last frame; music cut on a bar boundary.
faceless.compliance:
- Label fiction as fiction (chat stories). No real people's faces or voices without consent. Realistic AI media gets `ai_disclosure`.
- Run `originality_check` against the last 20 episodes and `policy_check` before the final render.

talking_head._intro:
# Talking-head edit rulebook

Format: one or two people speaking to camera. House rules, not platform rules. Each section is served separately by `get_rulebook`.
talking_head.workflow:
1. `footage_ingest` every take. Read the transcript pack, never the raw video.
2. Load the edit style (`edit_style_get`) or create one from a reference the user has rights to (`edit_style_create`).
3. `edit_plan_create`: select registry decisions per range, apply with `apply_decisions`, validate (F1 to F7), show the decision log, wait for approval.
4. Captions (`caption_apply_style` with face avoidance), music and SFX, brand overlays, then `render_preview`, `qa_check`, approval, `render_final`.
talking_head.pacing:
- Open on the strongest self-contained line (`cut_pacing.hook_first`). The proposition should be clear within 3 s.
- Remove dead air over about 450 ms and fillers; keep about 160 ms of breathing room so speech stays natural.
- A visual change (cut, punch-in, crop change, overlay) at least every 2.5 s in short-form, every 5 s in long-form.
- Cut on sentence boundaries. Never cut inside a word (F1). Every cut gets a 30 ms audio crossfade (F2).
talking_head.framing:
- Vertical reframe follows the face with smoothing around 0.85 and headroom about 12 percent of frame height.
- Alternate two framings (A wide, B about 15 percent tighter) across cuts to simulate two cameras.
- Punch-ins of 1.08 to 1.25 on stressed words, at most about 10 per minute, never within 300 ms of a shot edge, face stays inside the safe zone (F3).
talking_head.captions:
- Default preset `mino_clean_3word` (or the brand kit preset): 2 to 3 words per page, white, soft shadow, no animation, kept clear of platform buttons.
- Captions never cover the face (F4): shift within `universal_relaxed`, else fewer lines, else hide and warn.
- Hide captions while on-screen text occupies the same area.
talking_head.audio:
- Voice first: denoise lightly, loudness to -14 LUFS integrated, true peak -1 dBTP.
- Music 16 to 20 dB under the voice, ducked on speech, cut or drop at the hook end, bar-aligned loop or fade.
- SFX sparingly: whoosh on transitions, pop on text-in, click on counters, at least 300 ms apart, never on a key word.
talking_head.brand:
- Lower third at the first appearance of each speaker, 3 to 4 s, from the brand kit.
- Logo bug in a safe-zone-aware corner, low opacity. No other app's logos or watermarks.
- Intros eat hook time: default off for short-form; outro or end card at most 1.5 s with a single CTA.
talking_head.export:
- Master at CRF 18 to 20, H.264 yuv420p, AAC 48 kHz. One variant per platform preset, re-validated per target.
- Attach sidecar SRT and VTT. Write the receipt and the attribution file.

recipe_faceless_short.name: recipe_faceless_short
recipe_faceless_short.title: Faceless short (code-driven)
recipe_faceless_short.description: End-to-end chain for a faceless 9:16 video from idea to export package, with checkpoints at script, wireframe and preview.

args.topic: What the video is about (one sentence)

recipe_faceless_short.body:
Follow these skills in order. `checkpoint` means show the artifact and wait for approval before continuing. Use `run_state` so a rerun skips completed steps.

1. `local_env_check` (first run only), then `project_create` if no project folder exists.
2. `idea_generate` -> `script_write` -> `hook_generate` (pick 1, keep 2 for A/B) -> `hook_grade` -> `script_tighten` -> checkpoint: script.
3. `variation_pick` -> `scene_plan_create`.
4. `tts_generate` -> `audio_align` -> `music_select` -> `beat_detect` -> `beat_sync_apply` -> `sfx_place` -> `captions_build` -> `loop_seal` (if the format loops).
5. `scene_plan_validate` -> `wireframe_render` -> checkpoint: wireframe.
6. `render_preview` -> `qa_check` -> checkpoint: preview.
7. `originality_check` -> `policy_check` -> `render_final` -> `qa_check`.
8. `cover_frame` -> `metadata_write` -> `export_package` -> `publish_checklist`.

Inputs for this run: topic "{{topic}}", style pack "{{style_pack_id}}", target length {{target_s}} s.

recipe_talking_head_edit.name: recipe_talking_head_edit
recipe_talking_head_edit.title: Talking-head edit (local footage)
recipe_talking_head_edit.description: Edit one or more talking-head takes on the user's machine: ingest, style, decisions, captions, brand, render. Footage never leaves the computer.

args.edit_style_id: Saved edit style id (optional; otherwise create one from a reference)

recipe_talking_head_edit.body:
1. `local_env_check`, `goals_intake` (if the project has no goals).
2. `footage_ingest` on {{footage_paths}} -> `edit_style_get` {{edit_style_id}} (or `edit_style_create` from a reference the user has rights to) -> `edit_rulebook_get` talking_head.
3. `edit_plan_create` -> checkpoint: edit plan and decision_log.
4. `caption_apply_style` -> `sfx_music_auto_place` (`music_select`, `sfx_place`, `audio_mix`) -> brand overlays (`lower_third_apply`, `logo_bug_apply`).
5. `scene_plan_validate` (rules incl. F1 to F7) -> `render_preview` -> `qa_check` -> checkpoint: preview.
6. `render_final` -> `cover_frame` or `thumbnail_talking_head` -> `metadata_write` -> `export_package`.

Target length {{target_s}} s. Report `analysis_depth` honestly if any input came from a link.

{
  "$comment": "Templates are paraphrased patterns, not measured performance. hook_library_search returns a pattern plus a paraphrase, never a creator's text for verbatim reuse.",
  "version": "2026-11-08",
  "types": [
    {"id": "curiosity_gap", "template": "What happens if you [X] every day for [N] days?", "fits": ["what_if", "cubestory"], "visual_hint": "Show the starting state and a hidden end state"},
    {"id": "shock_number", "template": "[Big number] [unit]. That's [relatable comparison].", "fits": ["data", "finance"], "visual_hint": "Number slams in at frame 0"},
    {"id": "contrarian", "template": "Everyone says [belief]. It's wrong.", "fits": ["explainers"], "visual_hint": "Strike through the belief text"},
    {"id": "direct_question", "template": "Would you rather [A] or [B]?", "fits": ["quizzes"], "visual_hint": "Two cards, versus layout"},
    {"id": "stakes", "template": "You have [time] to [task] or [consequence].", "fits": ["stories"], "visual_hint": "Countdown element"},
    {"id": "list_promise", "template": "[N] [things] that [benefit], number [N] is [tease].", "fits": ["listicles"], "visual_hint": "Numbered header with the last item blurred"},
    {"id": "in_media_res", "template": "Start at the climax, then: Let me back up.", "fits": ["storytime"], "visual_hint": "Open on the most dramatic frame"},
    {"id": "visual_pattern_interrupt", "template": "No words; an impossible visual in frame 1.", "fits": ["satisfying", "3d"], "visual_hint": "Physically impossible motion or scale"},
    {"id": "pov", "template": "POV: you just [situation].", "fits": ["chat_stories"], "visual_hint": "First-person framing"},
    {"id": "challenge", "template": "Bet you can't [task] before this ends.", "fits": ["quizzes", "loops"], "visual_hint": "Progress bar or timer"}
  ],
  "grading_rubric": {
    "clarity": "One idea, understood on first hearing",
    "specificity": "Concrete nouns and numbers, no vague promise",
    "curiosity": "Opens a loop the payoff closes",
    "visual_support": "A frame-0 visual that carries the hook without sound",
    "time_to_proposition": "Proposition is clear within 3 s (TikTok creative best practices, ads context)"
  }
}

    {"id": "format_specific.faceless_defaults", "category": "format_specific", "name": "Faceless defaults", "detector": {"kind": "always"}, "effect": {"op": "export_setting", "args": {"bundle": ["captions.preset_pop", "captions.emphasis_numbers_keywords", "music.drop_on_hook_end", "sfx.whoosh_on_transition", "sfx.pop_on_text_in", "hook_structure.text_hook_frame0", "export_platform.safe_zone_strict"]}}, "params": {}, "applies_to": ["faceless"], "source": "house", "default_on": true, "rationale": "Pacing and SFX density for code-driven video."},
    {"id": "format_specific.ad_ugc_beats", "category": "format_specific", "name": "Ad or UGC beat map", "detector": {"kind": "always"}, "effect": {"op": "export_setting", "args": {"beat_map": ["hook", "problem", "demo", "proof", "offer", "cta"]}}, "params": {}, "applies_to": ["ad_ugc"], "source": "house", "default_on": true, "rationale": "Problem, demo, proof, offer, CTA; captions on; CTA end card; claims list runs through fact_check."},
    {"id": "format_specific.screen_demo_cursor_zoom", "category": "format_specific", "name": "Cursor zoom on clicks", "detector": {"kind": "keyword", "args": {"words": ["click", "tap", "select", "open"]}}, "effect": {"op": "zoom", "args": {"scale": 1.6, "ms": 500, "easing": "ease_out_expo", "anchor": "cursor"}}, "params": {"scale": {"type": "number", "default": 1.6, "min": 1.2, "max": 2.5}}, "applies_to": ["screen_demo"], "source": "house", "default_on": true, "rationale": "Zoom to the click target; blur sensitive regions found by OCR (emails, keys)."},
    {"id": "format_specific.screen_demo_click_highlight", "category": "format_specific", "name": "Click highlight", "detector": {"kind": "keyword", "args": {"words": ["click", "tap"]}}, "effect": {"op": "overlay", "args": {"kind": "callout", "slot": "cursor_zoom", "primitive": "pop_in", "duration_ms": 500}}, "params": {}, "applies_to": ["screen_demo"], "source": "house", "default_on": true, "rationale": "Ring around the cursor on each click."},
    {"id": "format_specific.screen_demo_idle_trim", "category": "format_specific", "name": "Idle-time trim", "detector": {"kind": "silence", "args": {"min_gap_ms": 1500}}, "effect": {"op": "speed", "args": {"speed": 4}}, "params": {"speed": {"type": "number", "default": 4, "min": 2, "max": 8}}, "applies_to": ["screen_demo"], "source": "house", "default_on": true, "rationale": "Loading and typing stretches get sped up instead of cut so context survives."},
    {"id": "format_specific.podcast_speaker_cards", "category": "format_specific", "name": "Podcast speaker cards and waveform", "detector": {"kind": "face_present", "args": {"min_ms": 1000}}, "effect": {"op": "layer_add", "args": {"kind": "lower_third", "slot": "lower_third", "primitive": "slide", "duration_ms": 3000}}, "params": {}, "applies_to": ["podcast_clip"], "source": "house", "default_on": true, "rationale": "Speaker card on each change; waveform layer under the captions; cut-follow-speaker reframe."},
    {"id": "format_specific.long_form_chapters", "category": "format_specific", "name": "Long-form chapters and retention resets", "detector": {"kind": "topic_change", "args": {"min_gap_ms": 1500}}, "effect": {"op": "layer_add", "args": {"kind": "text", "slot": "top_title", "primitive": "mask_reveal", "duration_ms": 2500}}, "params": {"reset_every_s": {"type": "integer", "default": 90, "min": 30, "max": 240}}, "applies_to": ["long_form"], "source": "house", "default_on": true, "rationale": "Chapter title at each topic shift; a visual reset at least every 90 s."},

  ]

{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "error.v1",
  "title": "Tool error",
  "description": "Printed by every toolkit script on failure and used by validators for each issue.",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["code", "message", "retryable"],
  "properties": {
    "code": {"enum": ["INVALID_INPUT", "SPEC_INVALID", "ASSET_NOT_FOUND", "LICENSE_BLOCKED", "PROVIDER_ERROR", "RATE_LIMITED", "RENDER_FAILED", "TIMEOUT", "ENV_MISSING", "CONFLICT"]},
    "message": {"type": "string"},
    "retryable": {"type": "boolean"},
    "path": {"type": "string", "description": "JSON pointer into the offending spec field"},
    "fix_hint": {"type": "string", "description": "One actionable sentence the assistant can follow"},
    "details": {"type": "object"}
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
